data.name: Purnima
data.gender_notes: Purnima is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Purnima is derived from the Sanskrit words pur meaning 'full' and nama meaning 'name'. The name Purnima signifies the full moon night and represents completeness, fulfillment, and blessings in Hindu culture. The name Purnima carries the meaning “Full Moon” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Purnima usually hope their child will grow to embody full moon and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Purnima is a name that is deeply rooted in Hindu spirituality. It signifies the union of the divine Shiva and Shakti, symbolizing the ultimate fulfillment of spiritual longing. It is also considered a powerful name for invoking the blessings of the Goddess Lakshmi, who represents wealth, prosperity, and abundance.
data.etymology: Purnima belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Full Moon.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Purnima total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: Purnima holds immense significance in Hinduism as it marks the full moon night, celebrated as a festival and held in reverence. various rituals and customs are performed throughout India and among Hindu communities abroad, such as offering prayers and fasting, worshiping deities, and engaging in charitable acts. Furthermore, several Hindu festivals occur on Purnima, like Raksha Bandhan and Sharad Poonam, that strengthen family bonds and promote love and unity among people.
data.spiritual_significance: On a spiritual level, Purnima is deemed as an auspicious day and considered an opportunity for spiritual growth and purification. Many Hindus observe fasts, engage in deep meditation, perform religious rituals, and seek blessings from deities to attain inner peace, enlightenment, and enhancement of their spiritual life. For many into various spiritual practices like Bhajan, Satsang, Kirtan and Dhyan treated this day is also an opportunity to intensify their Sadhana under the soft and serene glow of the full moon. Purnima is believed to be a time when devotees' wishes are fulfilled, and blessings are received from the divine.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Purnima, meaning 'Full Moon', symbolizes completeness and wholeness in life. It is a time to celebrate and give thanks for the abundance and blessings received. It represents the enlightened self, overflowing with love and wisdom.

historical_references.reference: Purnima is the name of the full moon day in the Hindu calendar. It is also known as Poornima or Puranmashi. This day is considered auspicious and is revered in various Hindu traditions. It falls on the 15th day of the lunar fortnight in the Hindu calendar month of Sharada (September–October).
historical_references.context: Hindu calendar, full moon day, auspicious day, Sharada month

historical_references.reference: Another significance of Purnima is that it is the day when the river Goddess Ganga descended on Earth from the heavens. According to Hindu mythology, Bhagiratha, a sage, performed a yajna (a sacred fire ritual) to bring the river Ganga down to the earth so that the ashes of his ancestors could be immersed in her waters and attain salvation. The descent of the Ganga from the heavens onto Earth occurred on Purnima, making it an important day in Hindu mythology and culture.
historical_references.context: Mythology, river Goddess Ganga, descent from heavens, Bhagiratha, yajna, salvation

modern_usage.modern_context: Purnima, also known as Full Moon Day, is a significant day in the Hindu lunar calendar. It holds spiritual significance in various Hindu customs and rituals, especially the Tithi-wise Shiva Puja. On this day, devotees across the world perform Shiva Puja, which includes offering bael leaves, milk, fruits, and flowers to Lord Shiva. The day is celebrated with much fervor and devotion on various social media platforms, blogs, and YouTube channels. People share their experiences, photos, and videos of the puja and the offerings they make to the deity. In recent times, Purnima has also gained popularity as a day for meditation and spiritual practices. Many spiritual gurus and organizations conduct webinars and live sessions on this day to guide and inspire their followers. Overall, Purnima continues to be an important day in the Hindu calendar, celebrated with enthusiasm and reverence on various digital platforms.
